# Linguistic Metadata

Our genetic data was taken from a range of sources (see Supplementary Table X <!--# This will be a table of where the samples were taken -->). In each case. there was a variant of the question "What is your primary language?". In Y cases, language was inferred based on the location from which the sample was taken. All coding decisions on language names, locations, and the comparability of questions across samples are detailed in the script `processing/format_geneticdata.R`.

In the tables below, we list some summary statistics. A notable discrepancy is that there are more individuals with missing language families than missing languages. In three cases, respondents gave an answer of a language, but we cannot pair it to a language from existing databases. These are: Imani (n = 19), Eyagu (n = 1), and Kora (n = 1).


Linguistic decisions of note:

-   Paiwaian (n = 52) is a language which has disputed membership to TNG, and could also be considered as part of the Tereban family [@pawley2017]. We include this language as a branch of TNG.

```         
::: {.callout-note}
We could consider Paiwaian as Tereban. SP needs to talk to NE about the strength of evidence for doing this. 
```

-   We have one speaker of Orokolo, an Eleman language that is sometimes categorised as a TNG language. @pawley2017 write there is no evidence for this link. We do not categorise this language as TNG.

# Phylogenetic Results

## Genetic Data

This project leverages existing samples drawn from 14 papers, with an additional 7 unpublished samples. In total, we analyse a sample of 861 mitogenomes. See Supplementary Table XX for the original papers which details the sequencing technology used for each paper.

```{r}
#| echo: false

ref_count = metadata %>% 
  group_by(reference) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))

kable(ref_count)

```

mtDNA samples were sequenced using \[what technology?\] <!--# How was this done? Probably ask Franois-Xavier -->. Sequences are reconstructed from the Revised Cambridge Reference Sequence (rCRS). See script `processing/create_reference_genomes.R` for processing details. We split mtDNA samples into M and N haplotype groups for computational efficiency.

```{r genetic_data_processing, echo = FALSE, eval=FALSE}
if(!file.exists("processed_data/papua_n.fasta") & 
   !file.exists("processed_data/papua_m.fasta")){
  system("RScript processing/create_reference_genomes.R")  
}
```

### Duplicate mitogenomes

There are 190 individuals with duplicate mtDNA mutations that group in to 107 distinct sets (i.e. some individuals have identical mitogenomes to multiple people). Of the 107 duplicate sets, 53 matched pairs have mismatched language classifications.

For phylogenetic modelling, we do not include duplicate genomes, as the contain no additional information. We pick individuals at random.

\[How to deal with linguistic mismatches\]

## Phylogenetic model

#### Mutation Rates

We use a strict clock mutation. We determine mtDNA mutations rates from studies calibrating the human mitochondrial clock (@rieux2014, @fu2013). In both studies we consider the whole genome substitution rate. We take the mean mutation rate from both papers to determine our rate.

|             Paper | Estimated Mean Mutation Rate |  Estimated 95% C.I.   |
|------------------:|:----------------------------:|:---------------------:|
|    Fu et al. 2013 |        2.67 x 10^-8^         | 2.16 - 3.16 x 10^-8^  |
| Rieux et al. 2014 |        2.143 x 10^-8^        | 1.58 - 2.706 x 10^-8^ |
|         Used here |       2.4065 x 10^-8^        |          \-           |

: {Mutation rates from existing studied #tbl-letters}

#### MCMC Settings

We run all models for 175,570,000 MCMC iterations, storing every 10,000 iterations. We take a burn-in of 20% which leaves us with a posterior sample of 14,047 trees, using the BEAST2 LogCombiner tool [@drummond2007]. All valuable parameters have an ESS \> 200. We create a Maximum Clade Credibility tree (MCCT) using the BEAST2 TreeAnnotator tool [@heled2013].

The bModeltest results show 44.41% support for a nucleotide substitution model of the form 123323. This is a non-traditional substitution model which contains distinct parameters for the A-C transition; A-G and C-T transversions; and third parameters for the G-T transition, and the A-T and C-G transversions.

```{r}
#| echo: false
log = read.table("NCI/20240910_CBESbModelTest_ALL/top.log",
                 header = TRUE,
                 skip = 1219)

# remove 20% burnin
burnin = ceiling(nrow(log) * 0.2)
log.noburnin = log[burnin:nrow(log),]

ggplot(data = log.noburnin, aes(x = Sample, y = posterior)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  ggtitle("MCMC Trace of the Posterior",
          "With burn-in removed") + 
  ylab("Posterior") + xlab("")
```

# Inference Results

## Language Metadata

The aim of this project is to determine whether linguistic affiliation structures genetic diversity by calculating the probability of sharing a language trait within a genetic clade, and the rate of within and between group variance for all pairs of traits. Traits are analysed at two levels, whether the language spoken by an individual is Trans-New Guinea of not, and then breaking Trans-New Guinea speakers down into language clades. This means for the two analyses, we have two results.

1.  Presence or absence of TNG
2.  TNG Language Clade

```{r}
metadata = read.csv("NCI/20240917_RAll//TNGData.csv")

metadata$tng_words = ifelse(metadata$TNG == 1, "TNG", "Not TNG")
metadata$major_haplogroup = substr(metadata$haplogroup, 1, 1)

kable(table(metadata$TNG_Branch, metadata$major_haplogroup))
```

### Trait heritage

To estimate the fidelity of language transmission over time, we calculate the probability of two individuals sharing a language within a genetic clade, across multiple times point in the phylogenetic history. This calculation follow from [@lansing2017].

$$
P(i_l,j_l)|i_{g(t)}, j_{g(t)}) = \frac{P(i_l, j_l \bigcap i_{g(t)}, j_{g(t)})}{P(i_{g(t)}, j_{g(t)}} = \frac{\sum_{g=1}^{c_t}(\sum_{i,j\neq i}1_{cos(l_ig, l_jg) > 0})}{\sum_{g=1}^{c_t}n_g(n_g - 1) / 2}
$$

$c_t$ is the number of genetic clades at any point in history, for t generations. We assume 25 year generation times. $l_{i_g}$ and $l_{j_g}$ are the languages or language families spoken by individuals within genetic clade $g$. $1_{cos(l_{i_g}, l_{i_g}) > 0}$ is 1 if the ith and jth individual share a language, and zero otherwise. $n_g$ is the number of individuals in $g$.

We extend this model to calculate the probability that two individuals share a particular trait, rather than calculating the probability of sharing a trait on average. This allows a more fine-grained view of the language-genetic connection. This approach has been compiled in the function `trait_heritage` within the package `traitheritage`, developed for this project. The trait heritage package can be found at: <https://github.com/SamPassmore/traitheritage>

We calculate the trait heritage for a number of different traits.

-   Whether a language is affiliated with the Trans-New Guinea family or not (`TNG`)
-   Language clade of the individual (`TNG_Branch`)
-   Language of individual (`interview_language`)

As with [@lansing2017], we compare the calculated probability with a permuted probability to determine whether languages are more likely to be shared by chance. We calculate XXX permutations per analysis.

We apply the trait heritage function across a posterior of trees. Within each tree we calculate the probability from the data, and the XXX permutations. This analysis was performed with computational resources provided by NCI Australia, an NCRIS enabled capability supported by the Australian Government.

### Walking Distance

We calculate distance between individuals as the cumulative time using Tobler's hiking distance. We then look at three increasing time barriers that map onto approximate distances of marriage according to @amato1983 (Table 1), which states that marriages range from between 1 and 186 kilometers away, with closer marriages being more common. Assuming a baseline of flatground walking, 66km takes around 12 hours, Taking these distances, we look at marriages that are approximately 6 hours walk away, 12 hours walk away, and 24 hours walk away (not including breaks for sleeping).

### Trans-New Guinea structure

```{r echo=FALSE}
source("analysis/helper.R")

mcct_tree = read.nexus("NCI/20240910_CBESbModelTest_ALL/full_model-all.mcct.trees") 
mcct_depth = mean(adephylo::distRoot(mcct_tree))

language_probability = 
  read.csv("NCI/20240917_RAll/results/TNG_full_model-all.noburnin_languagefamily.csv")

# Because we calculate the probability per group, we need to make this generational average 
# for trait probabaility data. But for Permutations, the average is all that is calculated
# because of the computational memory issues. 
language_probability_agg = posterior_aggregator(language_probability)

# Summarise the posterior
posterior_summary = summarizer(language_probability_agg)
# remove results that are older than the MCCT tree
posterior_summary = posterior_summary[posterior_summary$generation_time < mcct_depth,]

permuted_probability = 
  read.csv("NCI/20240917_RAll/results/TNG_full_model-all.noburnin_permuted.csv")

permuted_summary = summarizer(permuted_probability)
permuted_summary = permuted_summary[permuted_summary$generation_time < mcct_depth,]

metadata = read.csv('NCI/20240917_RAll/TNGData.csv') %>% 
  mutate(PhyID = paste0(ID, "_", haplogroup)) %>% 
  filter(PhyID %in% mcct_tree$tip.label)
# metadata_n = metadata[metadata$PhyID %in% mcct_tree_mtdnaN$tip.label, ]
mcct_tree = keep.tip(mcct_tree, 
                            metadata$PhyID[!is.na(metadata$TNG)])

keep = metadata$PhyID[!is.na(metadata$TNG)]
mcct_tree = keep.tip(mcct_tree, keep)

tree_data = full_join(mcct_tree, metadata, by = c(label = "PhyID"))

#### plot 
p_TNG = tree_line_plot(tree_data, posterior_summary, permuted_summary, "TNG")
print(p_TNG)

ggsave(plot = p_TNG, file = "figures/TNG_N_probability.png", 
       width = 315, height = 335, units = "mm")

```

```{r}
probability_bygroup = language_probability %>% 
  mutate(clade_probability = numerator / denominator,
         generation_num = as.numeric(str_remove(generation, "g_"))) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(clade_probability)) %>% # remove NA clades. Usually occur because of singleton clades
  group_by(posterior, generation_num) %>%
  summarise(denominator_gen = sum(denominator),
            clade_probability = numerator / denominator_gen,
            mean.prob = mean(clade_probability, na.rm = TRUE),
            ci_hdi = bayestestR::ci(clade_probability), # 95% credible interval
            n_matches = sum(numerator)) %>%

setDT(language_probability)
```

## Stable Clades

We further test the correlation between linguistic affiliation and genetic clades by testing trait stability across the posterior sample of trees. To do this, each individual within a phylogeny is assigned a trait. For a particular phylogeny, we identify all genetic clades where the trait is the same between all individuals. We then look across the posterior of phylogeny and identify clades that exist in more than 50% of the posterior (i.e. are stable clades).

#### mtDNA N Haplotypes

```{r eval = FALSE, echo=FALSE}
if(!file.exists("results/mtDNA_N_stableclades.csv")){
  system("RScript analysis/stable_clades.R -t NCI/20240702_N_CBES_bModelTest/20240617_CBES_bModelTest_adj-papua_n.noburnin.trees -v TNG")
}

## Metadata

states_df = left_join(states_df, metadata[, c("ID", "gender")], by = c("label" = "ID"))

mcct_tree_mtdnaN = read.nexus("NCI/mtDNA_N/mtDNA_N-papua_n_daru_pruned.mcct.trees")

# clean IDs
metadata$ID = gsub("-.*","", metadata$ID)

# subset to taxa in the phylogeny
metadata_ss = metadata[metadata$ID %in% mcct_tree_mtdnaN$tip.label,]

# extract the trait of interest
trait = metadata_ss$Branch_Family
trait[trait == ""] = NA
names(trait) = metadata_ss$ID

# remove missing traits
trait = trait[!is.na(trait)]
trait_df = data.frame(states = factor(trait), label = names(trait))

# match traits and tips

plot_tree = ladderize(plot_tree)

nodes = sapply(stable_clades_summary$tips, function(x)

  as.data.frame()
colnames(nodes) = "node"
nodes$tips = rownames(nodes)

# nodes_df = data.frame(nodes = nodes, type = stable_clades_summary$state)

tree_df = tidytree::left_join(plot_tree, trait_df, by = "label") 

## set colours
```

### Pairwise Between & Within group variance

We do not only want to understand the probability of particular histories, but also rate at which histories coalesce. To do this, for each pair we calculate the probability of between and within group variance to understand at what point, according to the phylogeny, were two languages groups likely to have been one language group.

This approach extends some assumptions of the phylogenetic model. First, that all partitions are binary.

```{r, wb_N, eval = TRUE, echo=FALSE}
metadata_ss = metadata[metadata$ID %in% mcct_tree_mtdnaN, ]
trait = metadata_ss$TNG
names(trait) = metadata_ss$ID

# w_b = traitheritage::within_between(tree = mcct_tree_mtdnaM, generation_time = 25, trait = trait)
# 
# saveRDS(w_b, "results/Branch_Family_mtDNAM_CCP_withinbetween.RDS")
# w_b = readRDS("results/Branch_Family_mtDNAM_CCP_withinbetween.RDS")

w_b = 
  readRDS("NCI/20240715_R_N/results/TNG_20240617_CBES_bModelTest-papua_n.noburnin_withinbetween.RDS")
v_within = lapply(w_b, '[[', "v_within")
v_within = rbindlist(v_within, idcol = "tree")
v_within[,  generation_num := as.numeric(str_remove(generation, "g_")),]
v_within = v_within[generation_num < mcct_depth,]
setkey(v_within, trait)

v_within_av = v_within[, 
                .(v_within_av = mean(v_within)), 
                       by = list(trait, generation_num)]

v_within_er = v_within[,
                       .(CI_Low = unlist(bayestestR::ci(v_within)["CI_low"]),
                         CI_High = unlist(bayestestR::ci(v_within)["CI_high"])),
                       by = list(trait, generation_num)]

v_within_av = bind_cols(v_within_av, v_within_er[,c("CI_Low", "CI_High")])

# kainantu_chumbu_w = v_within[J(c("Chimbu-Wahgi", "Kainantu-Goroka"))]

v_between = lapply(w_b, '[[', "v_between")
v_between = rbindlist(v_between, idcol = "tree")
v_between[,  generation_num := as.numeric(str_remove(generation, "g_")),]
v_between = v_between[generation_num < mcct_depth,]
setkey(v_between, trait_pairs)

v_between_av = v_between[,
                         .(v_between_av = mean(v_between)), 
                         by = list(trait_pairs, generation_num)]

v_between_er = v_between[,
                       .(CI_Low = unlist(bayestestR::ci(v_between)["CI_low"]),
                         CI_High = unlist(bayestestR::ci(v_between)["CI_high"])),
                       by = list(trait_pairs, generation_num)]

v_between_av = bind_cols(v_between_av, v_between_er[,c("CI_Low", "CI_High")])

# kainantu_chumbu_b = v_between[J(c("Chimbu-WahgiKainantu-Goroka"))]

within_between_N = ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data = v_within_av, aes(x = generation_num, y = v_within_av, col = trait)) + 
  geom_ribbon(data = v_within_av,
              aes(ymin = CI_Low, ymax = CI_High, x = generation_num, y = v_within_av, fill = trait),
              alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = v_between_av, aes(x = generation_num, y = v_between_av), col = "forestgreen") + 
  geom_ribbon(data = v_between_av,
              aes(ymin = CI_Low, ymax = CI_High, x = generation_num, y = v_between_av),
              fill = "lightgreen", alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_classic()

within_between_N
ggsave(plot = within_between_N, filename = "figures/TNG_N_Withinbetween.png")

within_N = ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data = v_within_av, aes(x = generation_num, y = v_within_av, col = trait)) + 
  geom_ribbon(data = v_within_av,
              aes(ymin = CI_Low, ymax = CI_High, x = generation_num, y = v_within_av, fill = trait),
              alpha = 0.5) + 
  theme_classic()

within_N
ggsave(plot = within_N, filename = "figures/TNG_N_Within.png")
```

# Genetic and Linguistic Distance

```{r}
## Data from Greenhill (In Press) - the TNG Phylogeny
tng_tree = read.nexus("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phlorest/greenhill_inpress/refs/heads/main/cldf/summary.trees?token=GHSAT0AAAAAACVQEUVFLA644VO6A2VDHQC4ZYEWJKQ")

tng_languages = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phlorest/greenhill_inpress/refs/heads/main/cldf/languages.csv?token=GHSAT0AAAAAACVQEUVFAUYKHVFWGUJB3IOAZYEWJUA")

# remove duplicates for merging
drop.langs = c("enga_wapi") # from ID
tng_languages = tng_languages %>% filter(!(ID %in% drop.langs))
tng_tree = drop.tip(tng_tree, "enga_wapi")

glottolog = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glottolog/glottolog-cldf/master/cldf/languages.csv")

## N and M metadata
# mcct_tree object used from earlier
metadata$ISO = str_extract(metadata$interview_language, "(?<=\\[)[a-z][^\\]\\[]*(?=])")
metadata_gl = left_join(metadata, glottolog[,c("Glottocode", "ISO639P3code", "Family_ID",
                                                "Latitude", "Longitude")], 
                       by = c("ISO" = "ISO639P3code"))

metadata_gl = left_join(metadata_gl, tng_languages[,c("ID", "Name", "Glottocode")], 
                       by = c("Glottocode"), suffix = c("", ".phy"))


language_distance = cophenetic.phylo(tng_tree)
dimnames(language_distance) = 
  list(tng_languages$Glottocode[match(tng_languages$ID,
                                         rownames(language_distance))],
       tng_languages$Glottocode[match(tng_languages$ID,
                                         colnames(language_distance))])

# geographic distance
geographic_distance = geosphere::distm(
  x = metadata_gl[,c("longitude_hybrid", "latitude_hybrid")]) / 1000
dimnames(geographic_distance) = list(metadata_gl$PhyID,
                                     metadata_gl$PhyID)

genetic_distance = cophenetic.phylo(mcct_tree)
genetic_distance[upper.tri(genetic_distance)] = NA
genetic_distance = reshape2::melt(genetic_distance, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(genetic_distance) = c("Taxa1", "Taxa2", "genetic_distance")
genetic_distance$Language1 = metadata_gl$Glottocode[
  match(genetic_distance$Taxa1, metadata_gl$PhyID)]
genetic_distance$Language2 = metadata_gl$Glottocode[
  match(genetic_distance$Taxa2, metadata_gl$PhyID)]
genetic_distance$language_distance = NA
genetic_distance$geographic_distance = NA

for(i in 1:nrow(genetic_distance)){
  t1 = genetic_distance$Language1[i] %in% colnames(language_distance) # test1
  t2 = genetic_distance$Language2[i] %in% colnames(language_distance) # test2
  if(t1 & t2){
    genetic_distance$language_distance[i] = 
    language_distance[
      genetic_distance$Language1[i],
      genetic_distance$Language2[i]
    ]
    genetic_distance$geographic_distance[i] = 
    geographic_distance[
      as.character(genetic_distance$Taxa1[i]),
      as.character(genetic_distance$Taxa2[i])
    ]
  } else {
    genetic_distance$language_distance[i] = NA
  }
}

genetic_distance$same_langauge = genetic_distance$Language1 == genetic_distance$Language2

ggplot(genetic_distance, aes(x = genetic_distance, y = geographic_distance, 
                             col = same_langauge, size = language_distance)) + 
  geom_jitter()

ggplot(genetic_distance, aes(x = genetic_distance, y = language_distance, 
                             col = same_langauge)) + 
  geom_jitter()


```

```{r}
library(INLA)

genetic_vcv = ape::vcv(mcct_tree)
genetic_vcv <- genetic_vcv/max(genetic_vcv) 
genetic_vcv <- genetic_vcv / exp(determinant(genetic_vcv)$modulus[1] / nrow(genetic_vcv))

pcprior <- list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec", param = c(0.36, 0.1)))

gen_model <- inla(
  TNG_Branch ~ f(
    PhyID,
    model = "generic0",
    Cmatrix = genetic_vcv,
    constr = TRUE,
    hyper = pcprior
  ),
  data = metadata
)
```
